answer: A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. Every claim climbs the cipher of verified tasks, and a reviewer at the ledge re-runs the work instead of trusting the label. Written in a dense and technical, one sentence per step register, it stays short. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the anchor of payment, so volume alone buys nothing. The design leans on cross-signed proof-of-personhood, held in escrow until finality, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool.
